channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Australian Dollar advances above 0.7050 as US and Iran announce a peace deal
item.description: The AUD/USD pair gathers strength to around 0.7075 during the early Asian session on Monday.

item.title: US and Iran agree on peace deal to end war and reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said that the United States (US) and Iran have agreed on a deal to bring their nearly four-month war to an end, with both sides declaring the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon, Bloomberg reported on S

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: Fed, BoJ, BoE and RBA decisions take center stage
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) lost ground during the week, down 0.27% to trade near the 99.80 level as investors prepared for a heavy central bank calendar the following week.

item.title: South Korean Won: Authorities step up FX stabilisation push – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale highlights that South Korean authorities have launched a multi-pronged FX stabilisation package to address short-term USD funding stress and speculative pressures on the Korean Won.

item.title: US Senior Official: Iran deal secures Hormuz reopening, nuclear material
item.description: A senior administration official said on Friday that the Iran deal will guarantee long-term peace in the region. The agreement would achieve core US objectives and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The official said that the US would get enriched nuclear material and include an inspection regime.

item.title: United Kingdom: Growth resilience but softer inflation – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Sanjay Raja says the UK economy is tracking close to the Bank of England’s Scenario A, with stronger‑than‑expected early‑2026 GDP but a cooling labour market and easing price pressures.

item.title: Gold clears $4,200 as optimism on Middle East deal dents inflation woes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price consolidates above the $4,200 figure on Friday as market participants are optimistic about a potential US-Iran deal, set to be signed next week, according to newswires. Meanwhile, households in the US are becoming more optimistic about the economy.

item.title: South Korean Won: Supported by equities and hawkish BoK – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad highlights strong South Korean asset performance, with South Korean Won (KRW) outperforming and the KOSPI up sharply on AI-led semiconductor strength.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: RSI enters overbought territory as bears defend 1.4000
item.description: USD/CAD trades on the front foot on Friday as lower Oil prices weigh on the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) amid cautious optimism that the United States (US) and Iran could reach an agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness raises intervention concerns – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/JPY is steady but elevated, with recent gains already surpassing prior intervention-trigger levels. A 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike on Tuesday is widely anticipated, and markets price nearly one more increase by December.

item.title: Euro holds steady against the US Dollar as markets await clarity on a possible US-Iran peace deal
item.description: EUR/USD fluctuates between modest gains and losses heading into the weekend as traders await Tehran's decision on a possible agreement with the United States (US) to end the war in the Middle East. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1573 and is on track to post modest weekly gains.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Policy mix supports stability – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes that Chinese inflation remains subdued, with May Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 1.2% and core at 1.1%, while PPI has risen to a four-year high, suggesting weak consumer demand and margin pressure.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average takes Pakistan's word for it
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) climbed 0.6% on Friday, settling near 51,200 and outperforming the rest of the US majors on a day when the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slipped into the red.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds as traders switch focus to BoJ hike and Warsh’s first Fed meeting
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades near the 160.20 region on Friday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains slightly under pressure, while investors prepare for a key central bank week featuring the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) policy decision and Kevin Warsh’s first Federal Reserve (Fed) meeting as Chair.

item.title: Gold pauses recovery as traders await clarity on US-Iran peace deal
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates on Friday as traders await further developments on a potential US-Iran peace deal. At the time of writing, XAU/USD is trading around $4,200 after climbing to an intraday high of $4,246 earlier in the day.

item.title: Silver price firms on US Dollar weakness amid easing US-Iran haven demand
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $67.50 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.21% on the day. The white metal maintains a positive bias despite improving market sentiment driven by diplomatic progress between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: BoE expected to hold rates as economists split on next move – Reuters poll
item.description: A Reuters poll released on Friday found that the Bank of England (BoE) is projected to keep the Bank Rate at 3.75% at the June 18 meeting, based on a survey of 65 economists.

item.title: British Pound stalls as UK GDP shrinks, diplomacy boosts risk mood
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) turns negative against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after UK data showed the economy contracted in April, while rising prospects of an agreement between the US and Iran improved risk appetite.

item.title: US officials' comments on Iran negotiations put mild pressure on US Dollar
item.description: United States Vice President JD Vance said on Friday that Iran would not receive cash or released funds simply for signing a potential agreement, pushing back against what he described as false information surrounding a possible deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end Iran’s nuclear weapons prog

item.title: British Pound: Steady against US Dollar before key BoE and data – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the British Pound (GBP) is consolidating recent gains around 1.3400, with domestic risk elevated ahead of next week’s CPI, labour data and the Bank of England decision.

item.title: Euro supported by hawkish ECB rhetoric as British Pound struggles after weak GDP
item.description: EUR/GBP holds firm on Friday, with the Euro (EUR) modestly outperforming the British Pound (GBP) as weak UK Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data reinforced signs of a slowing economy. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 0.8633, up from an intraday low of 0.8625.

item.title: CEE FX: Risk-on bounce but policy still key – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes that headlines on a possible end to the US-Iran conflict triggered a risk-on move, helping Central and Eastern European currencies erase recent losses.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Overbought Dollar holds near 1.40 ceiling – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret observe that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is weighed down by weaker Oil prices linked to Iran peace hopes, even as improved risk appetite offers some support.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar dips as robust US sentiment, inflation data underpin US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5830 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.15% on the day as the US Dollar (USD) maintains a firm tone following a series of strong US economic releases.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish forecasts point to higher terminal rate – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s European Economics team, led by Andrzej Szczepaniak and colleagues, notes that the ECB delivered a 25bp hike to a 2.25% depo rate and unveiled more hawkish forecasts.

item.title: Bank of England: Hold stance extended as inflation risks linger – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists expect the Bank of England (BoE) to keep Bank Rate at 3.75% with a 7-2 vote as Greene joins Pill in calling for a hike. They highlight persistent inflation pressures, upside risks from energy and airfare, and softer demand.

item.title: Breaking: United States Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rises to 48.9 in June
item.description: Consumer confidence in the United States (US) improved slightly in June, with the University of Michigan's (UoM) Consumer Sentiment Index rising to 48.9 in the flash estimate from 44.8 in May. This print came in better than the market expectation of 46.

item.title: British Pound: Poised to fall toward 1.3100 against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad says GBP/USD has given back part of its US-Iran-related gains and is expected to fall to 1.3100 as United States (US) growth outpaces the United Kingdom (UK).

item.title: Federal Reserve: Warsh policy shift and inflation focus – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) strategists assess how Kevin Warsh may reshape Federal Reserve (Fed) policy.

item.title: US Dollar: Peace deal talk keeps support intact – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that a potential US-Iran peace deal has softened the Dollar, but DXY is still holding firm. He highlights that energy supply losses and inflation risks persist unless Oil flows freely through the Strait of Hormuz.
